title: Verbos Clave: Practice
description: Authored B1/B2 practice set for five workhorse verbs a parent reaches for daily: enfrentar (face), averiguar (find out), aprovechar (make the most of), superar (overcome/exceed) and alcanzar (reach/be enough). Each verb is drilled across its different senses so it becomes usable in conversation, not just recognisable.

lessons.summary: Five verbs that do a lot of work in adult conversation, each with more than one job. ENFRENTAR = to face something hard: 'enfrentar los berrinches'; reflexive with a, 'enfrentarse a un problema'. AVERIGUAR = to find out by asking or checking (not saber, which is already knowing, and not conocer): 'Voy a averiguar a qué hora abre.' APROVECHAR = to make the most of, with a direct object and NO preposition: 'aprovechar la siesta', 'aprovecho para ducharme', 'aprovechando que duerme...'. The reflexive aprovecharse DE means to take unfair advantage of someone, a different verb in practice. SUPERAR = to overcome ('superó el miedo al agua'), to exceed ('superó mis expectativas'), to get over ('ya lo superé'); superarse = to outdo yourself. ALCANZAR = to reach ('no alcanza el estante'), to catch up with someone ('te alcanzo en la plaza'), alcanzar a + infinitive = to manage in time ('no alcancé a verlo'), and the gustar-style 'no me alcanza' = it isn't enough (time, money, patience).

examples.spanish: No sé cómo enfrentar los berrinches todavía.
examples.english: I still don't know how to deal with the tantrums.

examples.spanish: Voy a averiguar si la guardería tiene lugar.
examples.english: I'm going to find out if the nursery has a spot.
I use nap time to take a shower.

examples.spanish: Por fin superamos las noches sin dormir.
examples.english: We finally got past the sleepless nights.

examples.spanish: Hoy no me alcanzó el tiempo para nada.
examples.english: Today I didn't have time for anything.
examples.note: gustar-style: the time is the subject

items.prompt: No sé cómo ___ los berrinches de la tarde.
items.promptEnglish: I don't know how to deal with the afternoon tantrums.
items.explanation: Facing something hard is enfrentar: enfrentar un problema, un berrinche, una etapa.

items.prompt: Mañana me enfrento ___ mi primera mañana solo con la beba. (preposición)
items.promptEnglish: Tomorrow I face my first morning alone with the baby.
items.explanation: The reflexive form takes a: enfrentarse A un reto, A un problema.

items.prompt: Prefiero ___ el tema ahora y no dejarlo crecer.
items.promptEnglish: I'd rather face the issue now and not let it grow.
items.explanation: Enfrentar is the opposite of avoiding: you face the issue head on.

items.prompt: Voy a ___ a qué hora abre la guardería.
items.promptEnglish: I'm going to find out what time the nursery opens.
items.explanation: Averiguar is the ACT of finding out (asking, checking). Saber is already knowing; conocer is being familiar with.

items.prompt: ¿Ya ___ cuánto cuesta la clase de natación? (averiguar, pretérito, tú)
items.promptEnglish: Did you find out how much the swimming class costs?
items.explanation: Averiguar is regular in the preterite: averiguaste. A very natural checking-in question between parents.

items.prompt: Me ___ ayer de que cierran el parque. Ahora tengo que ___ adónde ir.
items.promptEnglish: I heard yesterday that they're closing the park. Now I have to find out where to go.
items.explanation: Enterarse = news reaches you. Averiguar = you go and dig the answer out yourself.

items.prompt: ___ la siesta para adelantar el trabajo.
items.promptEnglish: I make the most of nap time to get ahead on work.
items.explanation: Aprovechar takes a direct object with no preposition: aprovecho la siesta. «Aprovechar de» is the classic slip.

items.prompt: ___ que duerme, voy a cocinar. (aprovechar, gerundio)
items.promptEnglish: While he's asleep (taking advantage of it), I'm going to cook.
items.explanation: Aprovechando que + clause is the everyday way to say "seizing the chance that…".

items.prompt: El vendedor se ___ de que yo no entendía los precios.
items.promptEnglish: The seller took advantage of the fact that I didn't understand the prices.
items.explanation: Reflexive aprovecharse DE = take unfair advantage of someone. Plain aprovechar (no de) is the positive one.

items.prompt: —Está tranquilo el bebé. —¡___ ahora y date una ducha!
items.promptEnglish: —The baby's calm. —Make the most of it now and take a shower!
items.explanation: The tú command aprovecha is how Spanish says "seize the moment": ¡aprovecha ahora!

items.prompt: Teo por fin ___ el miedo al agua.
items.promptEnglish: Teo finally got over his fear of the water.
items.explanation: You enfrentas a fear while it's still there; once it's behind you, lo superaste.

items.prompt: Ser papá ___ todas mis expectativas. (superar, presente)
items.promptEnglish: Being a dad exceeds all my expectations.
items.explanation: Second sense of superar: to exceed. Superar las expectativas, superar el límite.

items.prompt: Cada semana dice una palabra nueva: este niño se ___ solo.
items.promptEnglish: Every week he says a new word: this kid keeps outdoing himself.
items.explanation: Reflexive superarse = to outdo yourself, to keep improving.

items.prompt: Fue una etapa dura, pero ya la ___.
items.promptEnglish: It was a rough phase, but we're past it now.
items.explanation: Getting past a rough patch is superar: ya lo superé, ya la superamos.

items.prompt: Ya ___ el estante de los juguetes: hay que subir todo.
items.promptEnglish: He can already reach the toy shelf: everything has to go higher.
items.explanation: First sense of alcanzar: to physically reach something.

items.prompt: Con un bebé, no me ___ el día para todo. (alcanzar, presente)
items.promptEnglish: With a baby, the day isn't long enough for everything.
items.explanation: Gustar-style alcanzar: the day is the subject and you are me. No me alcanza el tiempo, no nos alcanza la plata.

items.prompt: No ___ a ver su primer paso: estaba en la cocina.
items.promptEnglish: I didn't manage to see his first step: I was in the kitchen.
items.explanation: Alcanzar a + infinitive = to manage (in time) to do something: no alcancé a verlo.

items.prompt: Adelántate con el cochecito, ahora te ___.
items.promptEnglish: Go ahead with the stroller, I'll catch up with you in a minute.
items.explanation: Alcanzar a alguien = to catch up with someone: te alcanzo en la plaza.
